en.name: Pandan leaves
en.summary: Fresh pandan leaves keep 7–9 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). The leaf is stiff and fibrous, so it survives freezing far better than a soft herb: a frozen blade goes straight into the pot.
en.pantry: No room-temperature timeline is published for pandan. The leaves are tough and waxy and will not wilt as fast as a soft herb, but in a warm kitchen they yellow from the cut ends within a couple of days and the vanilla-rice aroma goes with the colour. Since the leaf is used for perfume and then fished out of the pot, losing that aroma is losing the entire point of it. Wrap and refrigerate, or freeze.
en.fridge: 7–9 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below — a figure borrowed from lemongrass rather than measured for pandan. Wrap the bundle loosely in kitchen paper inside a bag in the crisper. The leaves keep better than a soft herb because of that waxy surface, but they still yellow from the cut ends as they go. Wash and dry them only when you are about to use them; a wet bundle in a closed bag will start to go slimy at the base.
en.freezer: 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and outside the tropics this is the sensible default. Rinse, dry thoroughly, cut into lengths that fit your pans, and bag them flat with the air pressed out. Frozen leaves are limp on thawing but the aroma survives well, and they can go straight into a pot of rice or a coconut syrup from frozen. Tie a knot in a length before freezing and it is easy to retrieve later.
en.thawing: Use them straight from frozen. There is no advantage to thawing, and a thawed leaf is limp and harder to knot or tie.
spoilage: Yellowing that has spread from the cut ends through the leaf.
Slimy patches, usually at the base of the bundle.
Mould where damp leaves were sealed in a bag.
No sweet, grassy aroma when a leaf is bruised or cut.
tips: Bruise or knot the leaves before cooking; that is what releases the aroma.
Freeze in pan-sized lengths so you can use them straight from the bag.
Wash and dry only at the point of use.
Pandan extract and frozen leaves are both better than dried pandan, which has very little aroma left.

faq.q: How long do pandan leaves keep?
faq.a: 7–9 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Both figures are read across from lemongrass.
Yes, 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and it is the sensible option outside the tropics. The leaves go limp but the aroma survives well.

faq.q: Can pandan leaves be kept at room temperature?
faq.a: No timeline is published for it. They yellow from the cut ends within a couple of days and lose their aroma, so refrigerate or freeze them.

zh.name: 香蘭葉
zh.summary: 新鮮香蘭葉放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 7～9 天，−18 °C 冷凍可放 6 個月。它的葉片堅韌、纖維多，所以比嫩香草耐凍得多：冷凍的葉片可以直接丟進鍋裡。
zh.pantry: 香蘭葉沒有公布的室溫期限。葉片韌而有蠟質，不會像軟莖香草那樣很快萎軟；但在溫暖的廚房裡，它會在一兩天內從切口開始發黃，而那股「香草加米飯」的香氣也跟著顏色一起走。既然這片葉子的用途就是提香、然後撈掉，失去香氣等於失去它的全部意義。請包好冷藏，或冷凍。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 7～9 天——這個數字是從檸檬香茅借來的，不是針對香蘭葉測出來的。請用廚房紙巾把整束鬆鬆包好，裝袋放蔬果室。因為表面有蠟質，它比軟莖香草耐放，但還是會從切口開始發黃。要用時才洗、才擦乾；濕著密封在袋子裡的一束，基部會開始變黏滑。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 6 個月；在熱帶以外的地方，這就是合理的預設做法。沖洗、徹底擦乾、剪成適合你鍋子的長度，壓出空氣平放裝袋。冷凍過的葉子解凍後會軟塌，但香氣保留得很好，而且可以直接從冷凍丟進一鍋飯或椰糖漿裡。冷凍前先把每段打個結，之後很好撈起來。
zh.thawing: 直接從冷凍使用。解凍沒有任何好處，而且解凍後的葉子軟塌，反而不好打結或綁。
spoilage: 發黃從切口一路蔓延到整片葉子。
出現黏滑的斑塊，通常在整束的基部。
葉子還濕就密封在袋子裡而長霉。
折斷或切開時完全聞不到那股帶青草的甜香。
tips: 下鍋前先把葉子拍一拍或打結；那才會把香氣放出來。
剪成鍋子用得上的長度再冷凍，就能直接從袋子取用。
要用的當下才洗、才擦乾。
香蘭精華和冷凍葉都勝過乾燥香蘭葉，後者幾乎沒剩什麼香氣。

faq.a: 4 °C 以下冷藏 7～9 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 6 個月。兩個數字都是比照檸檬香茅而來。
可以，−18 °C 下 6 個月；在熱帶以外的地方這就是合理的選擇。葉子會軟塌，但香氣保留得很好。
它沒有公布常溫的期限。一兩天內就會從切口發黃、失去香氣，所以請冷藏或冷凍。
